sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian often marks the possessor relationship directly on the possessed noun — either as a suffix attached to it, or as a stand-alone possessive pronoun built the same way.

Compare barátom (my friend, consonant-final stem) with szobánk (our room, where the vowel-final stem lengthens its final a to á before the suffix) — Hungarian possessive suffixes shift shape slightly depending on what the noun ends in. It's really the same small set of person-endings adjusting to fit smoothly onto the stem.
